item.title: Texas AG Paxton Offers to Quit Senate Race for Trump Election Bill
item.description: AUSTIN, TX — Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton said Thursday he would consider dropping out of his U.S. Senate runoff race against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn if Senate leaders lift the filibuster and pass a Trump-backed election bill he called the chamber's most important ever. Paxton, a Republican who advanced to the May 26 runoff after finishing second to Cornyn in Tuesday's GOP primary, praised the SAVE America Act as essential for President Donald Trump's agenda. Learn More Here.

item.title: Fire Prompts Road Closure on North Chadbourne Street
item.description: SAN ANGELO, TX — A house fire at Ninth and North Chadbourne streets prompted police to close a section of the road between Eighth and 10th streets Thursday afternoon. Learn More Here.

item.title: Wichita Falls School District Avoids Takeover by State
item.description: WICHITA FALLS, TX — The Wichita Falls school district will not be placed under state control, district officials announced at a Thursday board meeting.Under state law, when a single school receives five consecutive F grades on the state’s accountability scale, the Texas Education Agency can replace a district’s locally elected school board or close the struggling campus. Learn More Here.

item.title: Grape Creek ISD Locked Down After Wanted Suspect Flees Deputies
item.description: GRAPE CREEK, TX - Earlier today, deputies with the Tom Green County Sheriff's Office attempted to make contact with a wanted subject in the area of Grape Creek ISD. The individual fled from deputies on foot and was potentially on the grounds of the school. As a precaution, a lockdown of the school was initiated. item.title: No. 2 Mason Cowgirls Unable to Complete Comeback Against No. 1 Panhandle
item.description: SAN ANTONIO, TX — The No. 2-ranked Mason Cowgirls basketball team was playing in its first state championship Thursday, and it looked like it early.Mason fell into a 15-0 hole just minutes into the game against No. 1 Panhandle, and the Cowgirls trailed by as much as 21-4 early in the second quarter.
